response.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT orderslink, rebtotal, rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0) AS ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005 AND orderslink IS NOT NULL), per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM qualifying GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio / NULLIF(o.mean_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "Clears the 0.0005 threshold" means rebrate >= 0.0005 (inclusive). The request does not settle whether the boundary is inclusive.
Fee rows with a NULL orderslink are excluded, since they cannot be attributed to an order.
A zero or NULL feerate makes the ratio NULL (via NULLIF), so it is ignored in the per-order average instead of raising a division-by-zero error.
The overall mean is the AVG of per-order average ratios, so each order counts equally. Orders whose average ratio is NULL are left out of that mean.
The relative ratio is NULL when the overall mean is NULL. The NULLIF also makes it NULL when the mean is exactly 0, to avoid division by zero; the request did not mention this case.
The database is PostgreSQL, since the request relies on NULLS LAST ordering.

alternatives.interpretation: "Clears the threshold" means strictly above 0.0005 (exclusive), so rebrate > 0.0005.
